'''Anne Lise Broadbent''' is a mathematician at the [[University of Ottawa]] who won the 2016 [[Aisenstadt Prize]] for her research in [[quantum computing]], [[quantum cryptography]], and [[quantum information]].{{r|aisenstadt|mathpeep}} As of July 2024, she holds the Tier 1 Canada Research Chair in Quantum Communications and Cryptography.{{r|crc}}
==Early life and education==
Broadbent specialised in music at [[École secondaire publique De La Salle|De La Salle High School]] in [[Ottawa]], graduating in 1997. Her interest in science led her to major in mathematics for her undergraduate degree.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-01-28|title=Anne Broadbent, scientifique superstar|url=https://www.ledroit.com/actualites/ottawa/anne-broadbent-scientifique-superstar-71fa9ce6beb5561d2351b82272fefa50|access-date=2021-04-30|website=Le Droit|language=fr}}</ref>

Broadbent was a student of Alain Tapp and [[Gilles Brassard]] at the [[Université de Montréal]], where she completed her master's in 2004 in the topic of ''Quantum pseudo-telepathy games'',<ref>{{Cite book|last=Broadbent|first=Anne Lise|url=http://hdl.handle.net/1866/14563|title=Quantum pseudo-telepathy games|date=2004|hdl=1866/14563 |oclc=969916927}}</ref> and her Ph.D. in 2008 with a dissertation on ''Quantum nonlocality, cryptography and complexity''.{{r|aisenstadt|mgp}}<ref>{{Cite book|last=Broadbent|first=Anne Lise|url=http://hdl.handle.net/1866/6448|title=Quantum nonlocality, cryptography and complexity|date=2008|hdl=1866/6448 |oclc=969910426}}</ref> 

== Career ==
After postdoctoral studies at the Institute for Quantum Computing at the [[University of Waterloo]], she moved to Ottawa in 2014.{{r|aisenstadt}} She is a Full Professor at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics of the University of Ottawa.{{r|uo}} From 2014 to 2024, she held the University of Ottawa University Research Chair in Quantum Information Processing.{{r|urc}}
==Awards==
Broadbent is the winner of the 2010 [[John Charles Polanyi]] Prize in Physics of the Council of Ontario Universities.{{r|aisenstadt|polanyi}} She was awarded the Aisenstadt Prize by International Scientific Advisory Committee of the [[Centre de Recherches Mathématiques]] in 2016 for her leadership and work in quantum information and cryptography. In 2026, she received the [[John L. Synge Award]] from the [[Royal Society of Canada]].
